title: When does rotor cant pay on a small quadrotor co-designed with its motors and controller?
lede: research programme: fixed rotor cant on a co-designed quadrotor; cant cuts attitude error by 4.2–5.3° under INDI, geometric and PID control (10 of 10 seeds) and still wins every seed in RotorPy with canted rotors; in position hold it cuts yaw error 5–8°; on a rigid frame its side force hurts one horizontal axis (1.9–3.4× the other) whichever side the centre of pressure is on
summary: An open research programme (target IEEE RA-L) on when a fixed rotor cant angle pays on a small quadrotor once arm, propeller, motor headroom and attitude controller are designed with it. Milestone 1 found that the torque limits of seven earlier simulated steps understated yaw authority by 2× to 2.8×; cant still beat no cant by 4.8° RMS. Milestone 2 makes roll, pitch and yaw share one thrust polytope through an attitude-priority mixer (as PX4 and Betaflight do) and puts a price on hover power. Without cant the tuned vehicle saturates roll and pitch on 97% of steps and yaw gets nothing; cant's paired advantage grows to 6.08° (SD 0.28, 5 of 5 seeds). Pricing power at 0.3° per 100 W cuts hover power 4–7× for under 0.5° of error, but the chosen cant stays at 28–37° in 9 of 10 seed-arms (best of three CMA-ES starts), refuting the hypothesis of a small 5–20° optimum; cant still wins the priced objective in 5 of 5 seeds at 0.3 and 4 of 5 at 1° per 100 W. Single-start CMA-ES is unreliable on the polytope (2 of 5 seeds fell to low cant). Milestone 4 asks whether cant only patches a weak controller: with incremental nonlinear dynamic inversion (INDI) or geometric SO(3) attitude control co-designed in place of PID (10 seeds, three CMA-ES starts each), cant still wins by 4.18° (INDI), 4.88° (geometric) and 5.27° (PID) in 10 of 10 seeds, and INDI without cant is 4.02° worse than PID with cant in 10 of 10. INDI narrows the gap by 1.1° and mostly steadies the uncanted vehicle; the chosen cant stays at a 34–35° median under every law. Simulated; TWR fixed at 2; the power price is a swept modelling choice; mass, cost and motor fits and plant ranges are inherited assumptions; no hardware. Milestone 6 adds position hold with the side force derived from the allocation (sinα / (L cosα − κ sinα) per unit roll torque, √2 smaller than an earlier study used), 6 s episodes and a 3 m/s wind step. Cant cuts yaw error by 4.7° in 6 of 6 seeds and does not buy position. Whether the side force costs position depends on the sign of the gust's disturbance torque, that is, on where the centre of pressure sits. Under the inherited sign the force opposes the drag and costs nothing (0.96×); flipped, it costs 1.21×, past the hypothesis's 20% line (re-scored, not retrained). Cant still wins the composite in 4 of 6 and 6 of 6 seeds. Milestone 6b derives the rigid-frame case: drag at a centre of pressure above or below the centre of mass gives opposite roll and pitch torque signs, which the inherited model did not have. Retrained under either geometry (6 seeds), the side force opposes the drag on one horizontal axis and adds to it on the other: late-window position error on the hurt axis is 1.9–3.4× the other axis. The typical design loses only 3% overall (median), but one seed in six diverges on 1–2 of 64 episodes. Cant still cuts yaw error by 5.1–7.7° (6 of 6) and wins the composite in 5 and 6 of 6 seeds. The translation model and the centre-of-pressure lever are inherited and assumed (lever swept 0–2×). Milestone 5 re-scores the 60 milestone-4 designs, not retuned, in RotorPy with a canted-rotor wrench, motor-speed dynamics and rotor aerodynamics scaled from its Hummingbird model. Cant still wins in 10 of 10 seeds for every law under RotorPy aerodynamics (3.1–5.8°), and the six law × cant arms keep their order (ρ 0.94–1.00; ρ 0.88–0.91 over all 60 designs against 0.95–0.97 for the stylised simulator against itself). The pre-registered top-ten test fails (ρ 0.20–0.30), but the top ten are tied and the stylised simulator scores only 0.26 against itself on fresh episodes. The stylised model is 1–2° optimistic, most for INDI.
